prompt.adult: The Elder writes to the elect lady. In 1:4, whom did he rejoice greatly to have found walking in truth?
prompt.child: John was very happy about something he found. Who did he find walking in truth?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:4: “I rejoiced greatly that I have found” whom walking in truth?
prompt.older: In 2 John 1:4, whom did the Elder find walking in truth?

verses.text: I rejoiced greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, as we received commandment from the Father.

explanation.child: Look right after “I have found” in verse 4.
explanation.teen: 1:4 says why he rejoiced and how it matches what we received. Read who was found.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:4 says this was as we received commandment from the Father. 1:1 says he loves them in truth.
teaching.takeaway: He found some of your children walking in truth.

prompt.adult: In 2 John 1:5 the Elder pleads with the lady that what he writes is nothing new. In 1:6, what is love?
prompt.child: John says that what he is writing isn’t new. What does he say love is?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:6: “This is love, that we” do what?
prompt.older: What does 2 John 1:6 say love is?

choices.text: walk in kindness toward the strangers
walk in unity with one another
walk in prayer before the Father

verses.text: because of the truth which abides in us and will be with us forever:
This is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the commandment, that as you have heard from the beginning, you should walk in it.

explanation.child: Look right after “This is love, that we” in verse 6.
explanation.teen: 1:5 says the call is not new; 1:6 defines love first. Read the definition.
explanation.older: It follows “This is love, that we” in 1:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:5 is addressed to the lady and says the call is not new. 1:7 warns of many deceivers.
teaching.takeaway: This is love, that we walk according to His commandments.

prompt.adult: 2 John 1:10-11 deals with a visitor who does not bring the doctrine of Christ. What does the Elder tell the lady to do?
prompt.child: John warns about visitors who teach wrong things about Jesus. What should the readers not do?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:10: if anyone comes and does not bring this doctrine, what then?
prompt.older: In 2 John 1:10, how should such a visitor be treated?

choices.text: do not receive him into your house
do not let him speak in the church
do not eat or drink with him

verses.text: If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house nor greet him;
for he who greets him shares in his evil deeds.

explanation.child: Look right after “does not bring this doctrine,” in verse 10.
explanation.teen: 1:10 gives a condition and then two instructions. Read the first.
explanation.older: It follows “does not bring this doctrine,” in 1:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:11 says he who greets him shares in his evil deeds. 1:9 speaks of abiding in the doctrine of Christ.
teaching.takeaway: Do not receive him into your house.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: 2 John 1:8 tells readers to look to themselves so they do not lose what was worked for. What does 1:8 say they may receive instead?
prompt.child: John tells his readers to be careful not to lose what they worked for. What could they receive?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:8: “but that we may receive” what?
prompt.older: According to 2 John 1:8, what may believers receive?

verses.text: Look to yourselves, that we do not lose those things we worked for, but that we may receive a full reward.
for he who greets him shares in his evil deeds.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 1:11 warns about greeting a deceiver; 1:8 warns about losing and then says what to receive. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “but that we may receive” in 1:8.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:11 says he who greets him shares in his evil deeds. 1:10 gives the warning about such a visitor.
teaching.takeaway: That we may receive a full reward.

prompt.adult: 2 John 1:9 contrasts those who abide in the doctrine of Christ with those who do not. In the greeting of 1:3, how is the Lord Jesus Christ described?
prompt.child: John’s letter opens with a blessing from God and from Jesus. What title does he give Jesus there?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:3: from the Lord Jesus Christ, who is what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:9, how does 1:3 describe the Lord Jesus Christ?

verses.text: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with you from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
Whoever transgresses and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ does not have God. He who abides in the doctrine of Christ has both the Father and the Son.

explanation.child: Look right after “the Lord Jesus Christ,” in verse 3.
explanation.teen: 1:9 is about abiding in His doctrine; 1:3 names Him and then adds a title. Read it.
explanation.older: It follows “the Lord Jesus Christ,” in 1:3.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:3 sends grace, mercy, and peace “in truth and love.” 1:9 says the one who does not abide in His doctrine does not have God.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus Christ is called the Son of the Father.

prompt.adult: In 2 John 1:13 the elect sister’s household sends greetings. In contrast, 1:7 describes many deceivers who have gone out. How do they fail to confess Jesus Christ?
prompt.child: John warns that many deceivers have gone out. What do they refuse to say about Jesus Christ?
prompt.teen: 2 John 1:7: deceivers “who do not confess Jesus Christ” how?
prompt.older: Read with 1:13, what does 1:7 say deceivers do not confess about Jesus Christ?

verses.text: The children of your elect sister greet you. Amen.
For many deceivers have gone out into the world who do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist.

explanation.child: Look right after “who do not confess Jesus Christ” in verse 7.
explanation.teen: 1:13 sends greetings; 1:7 describes the deceivers. Read what they do not confess.
explanation.older: It follows “who do not confess Jesus Christ” in 1:7.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:7 calls such a person a deceiver and an antichrist. 1:8 tells readers to look to themselves.
teaching.takeaway: They do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh.
